environment: Development and production follow-ups in the Codex in-app browser; each section identifies its scenario.
method: Eight-second requestAnimationFrame window around an ordinary 18-tile actBattle move in the actual Battlefield component. Movement samples require a rendered data-moving=true actor. Selected-unit camera tracking enabled. No campaign persistence.
interpretation: Production forest movement at 100% passes the 60 FPS budget in daylight and night, including immediate movement after 300% to 100% zoom. Native-density scenery removes the measured zoom texture rebuild stalls. Whole-game locked 60 FPS, cold loading, zoom interaction itself, and large battles remain unverified.

movementPlanningFollowup.scene: Buenos Aires, night, 100% zoom, camera follow, 18-tile walk, development server
movementPlanningFollowup.change: Stop move-order Dijkstra search at destination; index scenery obstacle cells once per terrain state
movementPlanningFollowup.acceptance: Not locked 60 FPS; no proven browser tail improvement. Cold loading and broader scenes remain unverified.

base movement cost cached by terrain type within each search

changes: Keep cached scenery layers mounted when actors share an exact depth; hide cache while members interleave
Use asynchronous FileReader data URLs for SVG/PNG preparation instead of synchronous blob URL creation
productionAsyncRasterFollowup.measurementCorrection: Do not collect full DOM/AX snapshots during the sampling window. That inspection produced repeatable 58-67 ms measurement interference. Read only the small status output, then collect results after 8 seconds.

daylightRegressionBeforeConversion.attribution: BlobCallback; finer timings measured blob URL creation blocking for 695.7 ms and SVG blob preparation taking 1016 ms

productionAsyncRasterFollowup.scope: Buenos Aires, 100% zoom, camera follow, production static build; no full-page inspection during animation. Fixture includes route selection time before applying the command. Warm scenery; no broad cold-load or full battle acceptance.
verification: visual check retains scenery and roof cutaways
remaining: Large battles, forest movement, cold loading, rapid zoom

forestAndZoomFollowup.environment: Production static build, 100% zoom, camera follows selected soldier; Tucuman has six squad members.
forestAndZoomFollowup.method: Route selection runs in a separate Prepare route action. The eight-second sample starts before issuing the ordinary move command. Only the small status is read during sampling. No full DOM/AX snapshots during samples; no campaign saves modified.
changes: Queue bounds, cloning and definition preparation with raster work.
Keep fading woodland images separate from large static depth caches.
Omit redundant daylight brightness filters and share exact shaded tree textures at night, with a 32-entry reusable cache.
Reuse detached prepared scenery sources for resolution changes; retain higher resolution images when zooming out; debounce resolution preparation for 300 ms.
limits: Movement measurements do not prove a locked rate across all gameplay.
A 25 ms move-start frame remains in the forest.
Large combat, moving lights, other hardware and first-load coverage remain open.

onDemandRoutesFollowup.change: Compute and retain UI reachability only when a cursor target or conversation needs it; skip during blocking animation and clear the cursor after accepted movement.
limits: A 92.4 ms frame after zoom remains reproducible evidence against locked 60 FPS.
Warm repeat meets budget; this does not establish first-use, zoom or combat acceptance.
No claim of causal frame-time improvement without a matched baseline.

changes: Return oversized scenery images to the settled zoom density after an 800 ms delay.
Reuse a prepared image when the 16 million pixel limit makes its physical dimensions unchanged.
zoomCacheMemoryFollowup.cappedGroundIdentityAcrossZoom: Same rendered image href confirmed for the ground at x25 y48. The largest image changes identity because a different layer becomes the largest after downsampling; that initial comparison was invalid.
zoomCacheMemoryFollowup.rejectedTrial: Deferring all downsampling until actors stop did not improve frame tails and was removed.

verification.visual: Night forest, buildings, soldier, HUD and 100 percent zoom inspected.

zoomCacheMemoryFollowup.acceptance: Memory use improves after settled zoom; immediate movement during cache replacement still misses 60 FPS. No locked frame rate or matched causal frame-time improvement claim.

nativeDensityFollowup.change: Rasterize scenery once at native device density (maximum 3), independent of camera zoom. Release detached vector sources after preparation. Preserve actor, tree, control and effect rendering.
nativeDensityFollowup.tradeoff: Cached buildings and ground can look softer when magnified above 100%; normal zoom detail is unchanged.
nativeDensityFollowup.scenario: Production build; Tucuman forest; six soldiers; selected camera tracking; prepared 18-tile route; 300% to 100% zoom immediately followed by movement; eight-second sampling; no full DOM inspection during sampling.
nativeDensityFollowup.validation: 13 focused rendering tests pass; TypeScript check and production build pass. Screenshot reviewed at 100%.
limits: Moving lights and room reveal transitions
Frame time during the zoom clicks themselves
